title: Anomalous behavior of Wilson fermions in the presence of monopoles
authors: Manuel Cortina, Rajamani Narayanan, Ray Romero
abstract: Three dimensional compact U(1) gauge theory supports a finite density of monopoles at a fixed lattice gauge coupling. After showing evidence for the expected dependence on the lattice coupling of the density of monopoles, we study the low lying spectrum of a two flavors of two-component Wilson fermions as a function of the bare Wilson mass. The Wilson-Dirac operator that realizes the two flavors are hermitian conjugate of each other to restore parity invariance and the commutativity of the two operators expected in the typical continuum limit is not the case in the presence of monopoles for all values of the lattice gauge coupling. This results in an anomalous behavior where we see clear evidence for the presence of very small eigenvalues for a wide range of a particular sign of the bare Wilson mass. These eigenmodes are typically in one-to-one correspondence with the number of monopoles as defined by the gauge field and the spectrum associated with these modes are separated by a gap from the bulk in the asymptotic regime of the lattice gauge coupling. The eigenvalues come in pairs around zero and the eigenvalues of one sign couple to the monopoles while the modes of the opposite sign couple to the anti-monopole implying flavor symmetry breaking.
summary: This work studies how magnetic monopoles affect the electronic spectrum of fermions in a 3D U(1) gauge theory on a lattice. The key finding is that monopoles induce anomalously small eigenvalues in the fermion operator, which are directly related to the monopole density. This suggests a topological mechanism causing flavor symmetry breaking in the system.
main_problem: The paper investigates the anomalous behavior of Wilson fermions when coupled to magnetic monopoles within a three-dimensional compact U(1) gauge theory.
main_result: The presence of monopoles leads to anomalously small, exponentially decaying eigenvalues in the fermion spectrum, with the number of these eigenvalues corresponding to the monopole density, indicating flavor symmetry breaking.
method: The analysis uses lattice gauge theory techniques, studying the low-lying spectrum of the Wilson-Dirac operator and relating its behavior to the monopole density.
model_or_system: The system is a three-dimensional compact U(1) gauge theory regularized on a lattice, probed by two flavors of two-component Wilson fermions.
key_observables: Low-lying eigenvalues of the Wilson-Dirac operator, monopole density ($ho_M$), and the fermion condensate ($\Sigma_f$).
important_parameters: Lattice gauge coupling ($ eta$), bare Wilson mass ($m_w$), and lattice size ($L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the monopole density can be calculated independently and that the small eigenvalues are localized at monopole/anti-monopole sites.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of monopole density and action density on $ eta$, and show the exponential decay of low-lying eigenvalues as a function of lattice size $L$ and Wilson mass $m_w$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the existence and density of monopoles in the U(1) theory. It then analyzes the fermion spectrum, demonstrating that the presence of monopoles causes specific eigenvalues to approach zero, correlating this behavior with the monopole count.
why_interesting: The study of fermion zero modes coupled to topological defects (monopoles) is a fundamental topic in condensed matter and high-energy physics, relevant to understanding topological superconductivity or fractionalization in strongly correlated systems.
